atoms.b: Air from your surroundings enters your nose through the ((++nostrils iris)). It lands on the moist ((++mucous_membrane pupil)) inside. This is about the size of a penny.

end.text: Mucous membranes line many of the cavities and organs in the human body. They are made up of cells that produce mucus to keep themselves moist and protected.

atoms.b: Millions of olfactory cells pass information about chemicals in the air to the brain via the ((++olfactory_bulb ear_canal)). The brain produces the impression of a scent, and we ((++smell see)).

hint.text: Olfactory means “linked to the sense of smell”.

hint.text: Smells can produce feelings, bring back memories and warn us of dangers, such as rotten food or fire. What we experience when we smell something is not just determined by the chemicals in the air, but above all by the feelings and memories that the brain associates with this smell.

instruction.text: What do people often associate with these smells?
